correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs periodic points of the compact closure (the dyadic cycles and all-zero configuration), since escaping periods contribute only singleton or zero nonperiodic limits. Distinct words with two or more 1s determine their dyadic gap; N-period singleton placements cover exactly N-r positions, while the other 2r singletons first enter at 2N. The all-zero and period-one all-one blocks give h(1)=2 even at n=1. Summation gives exactly 2n words and first/second moment geometric identities; summably weighted dyadic atoms yield the phase family and differentiation of m(t)=2/t-4/(3t²) gives endpoints 2/3, maximum 3/4 at t=4/3. All n>=1 including n a power of two are covered, and the normalized variance q(t)-m(t)^2 is explicitly justified.

final_claim: For the closure of all dyadic-spaced one-marker binary periodic orbits, every length-n cylinder has a periodic extension and the exact shortest-period histogram is h(1)=2, h(2^j)=2^j for j=1..floor(log2 n), h(2N)=2(n-N); the uniform-distinct-word period/n law has a nonconstant dyadic-phase weak limit, normalized mean cluster interval [2/3,3/4], and explicit variance phase.
